key_insight: Deeper symmetry-preserving VQE circuits can suffer an optimization collapse, while warm starts remove that collapse without guaranteeing the exact ground state.
engineering_relevance: Identity-layer warm starts can stabilize depth scaling, but low energy and singlet character alone are insufficient indicators of ground-state accuracy.
method: Study 10- and 12-site frustrated J1–J2 Heisenberg rings using a Néel-initialized SingleExcitationMinus ansatz.
Compare random initialization with chained warm starts that append identity layers to optimized circuits.
Track fidelity, energy error, half-chain entropy and total spin across circuit depths.
evidence_signal: Random initialization shows abrupt degradation near depth 9 for 10 sites and depths 10–12 for 12 sites; warm starts remove the collapse but stall at approximately 0.50–0.58 fidelity in some frustration regimes.
watch_item: Results are limited to the studied sizes and frustration values; nested circuits and finite gradients support an optimization-failure explanation rather than lost expressibility or a barren plateau.
paper_title: Depth-Dependent Collapse and Warm-Start Limits of a Symmetry-Preserving VQE for the J$_1$--J$_2$ Heisenberg Ring
